results.title: CISA and partners issue ransomware advisory on SafePay threat actors impacting critical infrastructure sectors
results.description: The Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency has published a ransomware advisory with the FBI and international partners detailing the activities of SafePay, a threat group hitting businesses and critical infrastructure sectors around the world using legitimate access controls. “SafePay is one of the most active ransomware groups and have affected businesses and critical infrastructure in North America, South America, Europe, and Australia--including at least 600 organizations from multiple critical infrastructure sectors since August 2024,” CISA said in an Oct. 20 alert on the advisory. The advisory says, “SafePay actors typically gain access to networks by stealing or guessing passwords, exploiting vulnerabilities in security systems, and using phishing tactics. Once inside the network, SafePay actors establish control by creating new accounts or taking over existing ones.” “They then use legitimate system tools to move through the network, identify valuable files, and disable security protections to avoid detection. Following, they encrypt the victim’s files, making them inaccessible, and leave a ransom note demanding payment in cryptocurrency,” according to the advisory. CISA acting cyber chief Chris Butera said in an Oct. 20 release, “Public-facing devices with known vulnerabilities continue to be frequently targeted by threat actors like SafePay Ransomware group. With our partners, CISA encourages organizations to review and implement recommended mitigations to include urgently patching the known exploited vulnerabilities in this advisory and conducting forensic triage to determine if systems have been compromised.” The advisory contains indicators of compromise, as well as tactics and techniques mapped to the MITRE ATT&CK framework. To mitigate the threat, the advisory provides a series of recommendations aligned with CISA’s cross-sector performance goals. The recommendations include regularly patching and updating systems, implementing zero trust principles and to restrict access to administrative tools and “privileges to necessary users only.” CISA also recommends taking steps to “[s]trengthen account security by implementing identity, credential, and access management (ICAM) policies and multifactor authentication (MFA).” “Today, the FBI and our partners are giving network defenders clear, actionable guidance to protect their organizations from one of 2026’s most active ransomware groups,” Brett Leatherman, assistant director of the FBI’s Cyber Division, said in the release. The advisory is supported by the FBI, the Secret Service and cyber agencies in Germany and the United Kingdom. -- Sara Friedman (sfriedman@iwpnews.com) Article Type: Daily News Sara Friedman tags: ransomware Weight: -20
